title: Console per-model chart inaccuracies when combining rate-limit exemption filters with quota buckets
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Console charts show inconsistent per-model token counts when users enable the 'Exclude rate-limited requests' filter together with a quota-bucket breakdown (e.g., reserved vs burst). Root cause hypothesis: two parallel aggregation paths (streaming event pipeline and periodic materialized rollups) apply the rate-limit exemption flag at different stages, causing partial deduplication and misattribution across model buckets.

Impact: dashboards for several enterprise customers report differences of ~0.4-2.5% in per-model token totals for windows with heavy retry traffic. This affects troubleshooting, quota reconciliation, and customer billing investigations. Not a systemic overbilling on hosted contracts today, but it increases noise for Reserved customers and complicates Dedicated capacity capacity planning.

Goals:
- Produce reproducible regression and a short demo dataset for the Console QA team.
- Fix aggregation ordering so exemption filters are applied deterministically before bucket attribution.
- Add parity tests between streaming and daily rollup paths to prevent regressions.
- Mitigate/patch live dashboards with a reconciliation overlay while the fix rolls out.

Scope: affects Console per-model breakdowns and any API that supports both 'exclude_rate_limited' and 'quota_bucket' filters. Does not affect raw billing sink events; those are correct.

Next steps: see comments for investigation notes and planned tasks.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ava Chen: Initial report from Customer Success: discrepancy surfaced after a customer ran a quota audit. Provided sample time ranges and model IDs. CS attached support ticket #CS-7784.

2025-02-12 - Ronan Patel: Reproduced locally with synthetic load. Observed that streaming-aggregator applies rate_limit_exempt at merge time, while daily-rollup service applies it during shard-merge. When retries arrive out-of-order the exemption flag can be lost, causing the same request to appear in both 'reserved' and 'burst' buckets.

2025-02-14 - Mei Alvarez (Data Eng): Ran a backfill on staging with instrumented flags; confirmed asymmetry on 2025-02-10 02:00-04:00 UTC window. Attached query: https://internal.redwood/analytics/queries/qa-ramps-104842

2025-02-18 - Ronan Patel: PoC fix pushed to branch fix/eng-104842-aggregation-ordering. The change canonicalizes 'rate_exempt' into event-level header before any routing/partitioning. Needs load testing on canary cluster. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/19762

2025-02-21 - SRE: Canary ran for 6 hours under synthetic retry workload (50% retries). No negative perf impact; observed corrected parity between streaming and rollups in canary namespace. Monitoring alert created: alert/console-aggregation-deviation.

2025-02-24 - Product (Lara Nguyen): Recommend adding UI note for customers explaining that a reconciliation overlay will be shown for 48 hours after any backfill/retrospective ingestion to avoid confusion.

2025-03-01 - Ronan Patel: Preparing rollout plan for runtime-1.20. Plan: deploy to staging, run 24h synthetic traffic, schedule production deploy during low-traffic window with expedited rollback playbook. Also added unit/integration tests to the analytics repo. Update: assigned estimate adjusted after load test discovery.
